prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1317; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the policyholder's household member, who was driving at the time of a low-speed head-on collision. The driver is covered as a household member under the policy, and the claimant has retained a lawyer who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Vehicle inspection completed. The damage matches the described impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 3: Police report and people at the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle. Photos from the scene confirm some details of the collision, but no independent witness saw the impact itself.

Entry 4: Claimant's medical records show neck and back strain, which is a plausible injury for a crash of this type. Records also show no earlier injury to the same body area.

Entry 5: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. The account differs from the first notice in the direction of impact and in the number of people in the car, and this has been noted for follow-up with counsel.

Entry 6: Treatment has continued to grow well beyond what this injury usually requires, with more visits and new services added each month. Medical review requested to assess whether the scope of care matches the injury, and the claim remains open pending that review.
